question.worked_solution:
For this integral, we choose $u=2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+5$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same Color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+5$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ |  |  |
| $6{x}^{2}+6x$ | $-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ | $+$ | $-(2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+5)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ |
| $12x+6$ | $-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ | $-$ | $(6{x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ |
| $12$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ | $+$ | $(12x+6)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ |
| $0$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ | $-$ | $-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+5)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-(2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+5)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+(6{x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\  & \,\,\,+(12x+6)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C \\  & =-(2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-12x-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\  & \,\,\,+(6{x}^{2}+6x-12)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$
